title: Elements of nonnegative valuation lie in the DVR
statement: Let B be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field K and normalized valuation v:K^\times\to\mathbf Z. If x\in K^\times satisfies v(x)\ge0, then x\in B.

source.place: Algebra Definition 00IE (algebra-definition-value-group): a DVR is the valuation ring of its valuation, B = \{0\}\cup\{x\in K^\times : v(x)\ge0\}

mathlib_searches.query: element of fraction field of discrete valuation ring with valuation at most one (nonnegative additive valuation) lies in the ring
mathlib_searches.results: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_lift_of_le_one (not in the pinned Mathlib: grep of Mathlib/RingTheory finds no such name); ValuationSubring.valuation_le_one_iff (Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/ValuationSubring.lean:183) is for the valuation subring's own value group, not the normalized Z-valuation

from.place: 09N5 proof, induction base case: a finite sum of elements of nonnegative valuation lies in the DVR B
